arabic_text: رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ، وَذَلِكَ أَضْعَفُ الإِيمَانِ
english_translation: Whoever sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart – and that is the weakest of faith.
question: According to this hadith, what is the first and strongest way a Muslim should respond when witnessing an evil action?

options.A: By speaking against it with the tongue
options.B: By changing it with the hand (taking physical action)
options.D: By disliking it in the heart

arabic_text: رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ، وَذَلِكَ أَضْعَفُ الإِيمَانِ
english_translation: Whoever sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart – and that is the weakest of faith.
question: In which authentic collection of hadith is this narration about forbidding evil found?

arabic_text: رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ، وَذَلِكَ أَضْعَفُ الإِيمَانِ
english_translation: Whoever sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart – and that is the weakest of faith.
question: What is the main Islamic principle taught by this hadith?

options.A: The obligation of commanding good and forbidding evil (al-amr bil ma'ruf wan-nahy 'anil munkar)
options.B: The importance of maintaining family ties
options.C: The obligation of performing the five daily prayers
options.D: The virtue of patience in times of hardship
